solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Labour having yielded, do this? Unite!

blocks.note: surface reading: a political party giving way and being urged to join forces
setter's reading: once childbirth has produced a baby, the old-fashioned advice is for the parents to marry

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to a defeated Labour Party to come together, with Unite the trade union lurking.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is not the party but childbirth: having yielded a baby, the couple is urged to wed. Unite is also a big British trade union tied to Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for getting married, the ultimate joining of two people.

clue.text: No. 10 possibly joining Eye readers? Get stuffed!

blocks.note: screws are sold by gauge number, and a No. 10 is a common size
the magazine addresses its readers, the readers of Private Eye, as you

explanation.surface: Downing Street telling Private Eye's readership where to go.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 looks like Downing Street, but it is a size of screw. Private Eye is the magazine this puzzle appears in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are rude exclamations of dismissal telling someone to go away.

clue.text: Gosh, getting pissed is a favourite personal ad requirement!

indicators.note: someone pissed is drunk, and a drunk's word comes out jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy exclamation, while noting what lonely hearts ads always ask for.
explanation.walkthrough: GSOH stands for good sense of humour, the stock demand of lonely hearts adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation appears in almost every dating advertisement as a quality the advertiser seeks.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) Smacker getting tongues wagging

blocks.note: surface reading: a smooch that sets off gossip
setter's reading: the tongues are literally moving

explanation.surface: A smooch that causes a scandal and gets everyone gossiping.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongues wagging is the idiom for gossip, but here the tongues are the kissers' own.
explanation.definitionFit: A smacker is slang for a loud kiss, and this is the open-mouthed variety.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Semi erection from this? Not ready

blocks.note: first meaning: literally a cock half up
second meaning: to act prematurely, unprepared

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase comes from a gun's hammer set halfway, where it should not fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something launched before proper preparation, and the literal reading gives the semi.

clue.text: A sign the Church is involved in leak

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be wrapped up inside it

blocks.note: slang for urinating, taking a leak
Church of England

explanation.surface: An omen that the clergy are mixed up in a leaked story.
explanation.walkthrough: Leak is slang for urination here, not a press leak.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fishes are one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Nigella's butt appears in educated woman's dish

indicators.note: a butt is the end of something, so only the final letter is kept
showing up inside something means sitting within it

blocks.note: the heroine of Willy Russell's play Educating Rita
the end of the cook's name

explanation.surface: Nigella Lawson's bottom turns up in a clever woman's cookery.
explanation.walkthrough: Rita is the working-class student in the play and film Educating Rita.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoghurt and cucumber side served with Indian food.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Miserable sort of tart, Fanny fails to climax

indicators.note: the climax is the end, and failing to reach it means the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: tart as in sharp-tasting
both are vulgar slang for the same body part

explanation.surface: A grumpy prostitute frustrated in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tart is an adjective for sharpness of taste, not a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: A sourpuss is a sulky, grumpy person with a sour face.

clue.text: Butter applied to middle of geek's facial hair

indicators.note: the middle of a word means its central letters

blocks.note: a goat is an animal that butts
the two central letters

explanation.surface: Smearing butter into a nerd's beard.
explanation.walkthrough: Butter here is one who butts, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed beard on the chin, named for its resemblance to a billy goat's.

clue.text: Don't touch Duke's dicky

blocks.note: dukes is slang for fists, from rhyming slang
dicky means unwell or faulty, like food gone off

explanation.surface: A warning not to grope a nobleman's member.
explanation.walkthrough: Put up your dukes means raise your fists; dicky is British slang for poorly, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The command is a warning against touching or interfering with something.

clue.text: Good side of character crushing resistance, Jock screwed Kelly

indicators.note: screwed up means mangled, so the letters get twisted around
to crush something you close in around it

blocks.note: a jock is a disc jockey
taken as written
symbol in electronics

explanation.surface: A tabloid tale of a Scot bedding a woman named Kelly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock looks like a Scotsman but is a disc jockey. Dr Jekyll is the respectable half of Stevenson's Jekyll and Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: In Stevenson's story the doctor is the decent persona, while Mr Hyde is his evil alter ego.

clue.text: Sprawling habit of novelist Jeffrey?

blocks.note: first meaning: stretched out flat
second meaning: telling untruths, for which Jeffrey Archer was jailed for perjury

explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, novelist and Tory peer, went to prison in 2001 for perjury.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both reclining flat and telling falsehoods, a dig at the convicted perjurer.

clue.text: Hello splash for the editor

blocks.note: a greeting
to spill or splash liquid

explanation.surface: A cheery greeting and a front-page splash for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Hislop is the long-serving editor of Private Eye, where this puzzle runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian Hislop has edited Private Eye since 1986, so to its readers he is the editor.

clue.text: Eye user, one enjoying dummy material?

blocks.note: one who sees
a baby sucks a dummy, a rubber teat

explanation.surface: A Private Eye reader who likes a bit of rubbish to chew on.
explanation.walkthrough: A dummy is the British word for a baby's pacifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Seersucker is a puckered cotton fabric used for summer clothing.

clue.text: With which a toady ends up ironically?

blocks.clueFragment: With which a toady ends up
blocks.note: surface reading: how a sycophant ends up, a riddle about flattery
setter's reading: an arse-licker literally finishes with his tongue on a buttock

explanation.surface: A wry riddle about how a sycophant finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheek is also slang for a buttock, which is where the toady's tongue goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something with tongue in cheek means saying it insincerely, with irony.

clue.text: Stuck up William, grabbed by throat, snapped "Pig!"

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means reading it from the bottom
something snapped is broken, so its letters fall apart
being grabbed means being held inside

blocks.note: standard abbreviation of the name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A snooty William is seized by the throat and someone barks an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Pig is the definition, as the Tamworth is a breed, though it reads as the insult snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamworth is a ginger British breed of pig, named after the Staffordshire town.

clue.text: It's unrefined, uncouth to puncture contraceptive

indicators.note: puncturing something means piercing into its interior

blocks.note: an intrauterine device
vulgar, ill-mannered

explanation.surface: A crude joke about sabotaging birth control.
explanation.walkthrough: The coil is the common British name for an intrauterine contraceptive device.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum straight from the ground before processing is the unrefined product.

clue.text: Flip quote by Cyclops causing vomiting

indicators.note: flipping something turns it end over end

blocks.note: the setter, Cyclops, asks you to quote him

explanation.surface: A flippant remark from the setter that makes people sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the me: quote by Cyclops is the setter saying cite me.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance that induces vomiting, used here as an adjective.

clue.text: Old bloke's penis needing a new opening

indicators.note: needing something means a part must be swapped in for what is there

blocks.note: British slang for the organ
a fresh first letter replaces the existing one

explanation.surface: An elderly man's member requires surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Todger is British slang for penis; its T is swapped for C.
explanation.definitionFit: A codger is an informal term for an old man, often an eccentric one.

clue.text: Possibly had a successful penis enlargement, said to be awful

indicators.note: said means the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.clueFragment: Possibly had a successful penis enlargement
blocks.note: after a successful enlargement, one has grown a bit

explanation.surface: A man boasting about surgery that turned out horrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome means horrible and repellent, a close synonym of dreadful.

clue.text: see 23dn.
Failed to get perverted decko inside part of bra

indicators.note: something perverted is twisted out of its proper form
inside places one thing within another

blocks.note: a bra has two cups
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peeping tom bungles an attempt to look down a bra.
explanation.walkthrough: A decko is British slang for a look, as in have a decko.
explanation.definitionFit: To cock up is British slang for making a mess of something, so cocked up means botched.

clue.text: (& 21dn.) After drunken lark maybe Thatcher's said to be a revolutionary thinker

indicators.note: a drunken thing staggers about, so the letters are disordered
said means the next part is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: taken as written
Mark Thatcher is the son of Margaret Thatcher

explanation.surface: After a boozy prank, the Iron Lady is called a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: Thatcher's is not Margaret's but her son's name, Mark Thatcher, plus an s.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Das Kapital is the archetypal revolutionary political thinker.

clue.text: see 9dn.
Euphemism for tart: "old banger"

blocks.note: first meaning: a paid companion, a polite word for a prostitute
second meaning: the Ford model, now a classic old car

explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a battered old car; the Ford model of that name was ubiquitous.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a hired companion and a once-popular Ford car.

clue.text: Brenda's taken in by the gutless Blunt

indicators.note: losing the guts means the inside goes, leaving only the ends
being taken in means being held within

blocks.note: the two end letters
Brenda is Private Eye's name for the late Queen, ER, plus the s

explanation.surface: The Queen deceived by Anthony Blunt, her art surveyor who was a Soviet spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye always called Queen Elizabeth II Brenda; ER is her royal cipher. Blunt reads as the spy but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunt remark is curt and brief, which is what terse means.

clue.text: Vigorous tosser's achievement secures victory for idle bugger

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside

blocks.note: in cricket a skier is a ball hit high into the air
V for victory

explanation.surface: A ruder reading of what a vigorous tosser achieves, beside a layabout.
explanation.walkthrough: Tosser is crude British slang, but here it is someone launching a ball skyward. A skiver is someone who dodges work.
explanation.definitionFit: A skiver shirks work, the very definition of a lazy layabout.
